channel.title: Long Island Business News - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Long Island Business News (libn.com)

item.title: Long Island aquaculture works to rebound after brutal winter
item.description: Long Island oyster farmers suffered major equipment and crop losses due to severe ice damage in winter.

item.title: Long Island Business News names 2026 Impact and Inclusion Award winners
item.description: Long Island Business News announced the 2026 Impact and Inclusion Award honorees recognizing leaders promoting diversity and inclusion in local workplaces.

item.title: PSEG-LI offers new round of business grants
item.description: PSEG Long Island offers up to $125,000 in business grants plus energy-efficiency rebates and upgrades to support local business growth

item.title: Fortunoff Backyard Store opening two relocated LI showrooms
item.description: Fortunoff Backyard Store is opening in Huntington Station and Stony Brook after relocating its Melville and Lake Grove Long Island showrooms.

item.title: LI hospital adopts 15-minute blood test to speed brain injury diagnosis
item.description: Hospital on Long Island uses Abbott’s i-STAT Alinity TBI blood test to diagnose brain injuries faster, reducing wait times and radiation exposure.

item.title: New Starbucks completes DRG’s reboot of Shirley center
item.description: Damianos Realty Group completed a $5 million renovation of Floyd Harbor Center in Shirley, culminating with the opening of a new Starbucks.

item.title: Medical practice to expand at former bank building
item.description: The 2,500-square-foot building on .64 acres sold for $1.5 million.

item.title: Breaking News: Matt Cohen to step down from LIA
item.description: Matthew Cohen is stepping down as president and CEO of the Long Island Association after 15 years, with Stacey Sikes named acting CEO during the transition.

item.title: Maltz Auctions to auction 50K cases of wine, liquor
item.description: Maltz Auctions in Central Islip will auction over 50,000 cases of wine and liquor from Apollo Fine Wine and Spirits, exclusively for licensed New York retailers and wholesalers.

item.title: Denied by IDA, spec industrial project still moves forward
item.description: Ares Management is moving forward with two speculative warehouse projects in Suffolk County despite Brookhaven IDA denying tax breaks.
